issues.t: Burning clutch smell from dual-clutch automatic
issues.sym: A hot, burning smell (sometimes light smoke from under the hood) in stop-and-go traffic or on hills, with slow or jerky take-offs and rolling back on inclines.
issues.why: 2014 500Ls with the 6-speed dual dry clutch automatic (DDCT) overheat their clutches when creeping in traffic. Dealers often called it normal, but some cars needed new clutches at low miles. Manual cars with heavy clutch slip show the same smell.
issues.next: In traffic, come to a full stop instead of creeping, and avoid holding the car on hills with the throttle. If the smell keeps coming back or the car slips, have the clutch checked while any warranty still applies.

issues.sym: A transmission overheat warning in slow traffic, high revs with a jerky engagement, the car refusing to leave Park, or the engine shutting off until it cools.
issues.why: The dual dry clutch design builds up heat in slow stop-and-go driving. Fiat treated much of this as normal, and some cars got software updates.
issues.next: When the warning shows, pull over safely, shift to Park and let it cool. Ask a dealer for all transmission software updates.

issues.t: Dual-clutch automatic shifts harshly or ignores shift requests
issues.sym: Hard, slamming or clumsy shifts, a shifter that is hard to move, manual-mode shifts that do nothing, and transmission warning messages.
issues.why: The dual-clutch automatic in early 500Ls had software and hardware problems; some owners needed repeated repairs. Fiat released computer updates to improve how it shifts.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the latest transmission, body and cluster software. If you are shopping, the later conventional automatic or a manual is the safer choice.

issues.t: Shifter may not select a gear (recall)
issues.sym: In some temperatures the shift lever may do nothing or select a gear late, so the car won't leave Park or moves unexpectedly.
issues.why: A fault in the shifter module on some 2014 dual-clutch cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the shifter module or update its software for free.

issues.t: Engine may stay at idle power when you press the gas (recall)
issues.sym: Pressing the gas pedal gives little or no acceleration.
issues.why: A wrong engine computer calibration could limit the engine to idle speed and power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers update the engine computer for free.

issues.t: Driver knee airbag may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning you would notice.
issues.why: The driver knee airbag may have been folded wrong at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the knee airbag for free.

issues.t: Passenger front airbag may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning you would notice.
issues.why: On cars built in spring 2015, the passenger front airbag may have been folded wrong.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the passenger airbag module for free.

issues.t: Dead battery after sitting a few days
issues.sym: The car won't start after sitting for several days, batteries wear out early, and after a jump start the ESC or check engine light may come on.
issues.why: Fiat issued body computer software to fix an intermittent battery drain on parked cars, and owners report early battery failures.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and ask a dealer for all software updates. Use a battery maintainer if the car sits for days.

issues.t: Engine won't crank and key stuck in ignition
issues.sym: The key turns but the engine won't start, and the key may not come out of the ignition.
issues.why: Owners report this no-start, sometimes after earlier battery trouble. A weak battery or an ignition or shifter fault can cause it.
issues.next: Check that the shifter is fully in Park and try a jump start. If it still won't start, have the battery, ignition switch and shifter checked.

issues.t: Engine oil leaks or low oil between changes
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell, or the oil level dropping between changes.
issues.why: Fiat has a bulletin for oil leak and oil use complaints. The 1.4L MultiAir engine needs the correct oil at the right level because its valve timing works on oil pressure.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every few fill-ups, use exactly the oil in the owner's manual and stick to the oil change schedule. Have any leak traced before replacing parts.

issues.t: Burnt valves or cylinder head damage on high-mileage engines
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light and low compression in one cylinder.
issues.why: At least one high-mileage turbo 500L needed a cylinder head after valves burned. Overheating or turbo problems were blamed.
issues.next: Have a compression or leak-down test done. Compare a head repair with the value of the car before agreeing to the work.

issues.t: Check engine light fixed by engine computer update
issues.sym: A check engine light with no clear drivability problem.
issues.why: Fiat released several engine computer updates for the 1.4L turbo for false or nuisance check engine lights and to improve starting.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Ask a dealer whether a software update applies before replacing parts.

issues.t: A/C blows warm or compressor fails
issues.sym: The A/C does not cool or blows warm air.
issues.why: Owners report A/C problems, including failed compressors.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and leak checked first. A compressor is the costly case.

issues.t: Climate control blows the wrong temperature
issues.sym: Cold air when you ask for heat, or warm air when you ask for cooling, from one or more vents.
issues.why: A sticking blend door, a failing blend door motor, or an electronic fault in the climate control.
issues.next: Have the climate control codes read. A blend door motor is usually the fix.

issues.sym: The big sunroof strains, binds or stops short, or the fabric sunshade tears, jams or falls out.
issues.why: Owners report problems with the sunroof mechanism and its fabric sunshade.
issues.next: Stop forcing it if it binds. Have the tracks and shade inspected.

issues.t: Grinding when shifting the manual into reverse
issues.sym: A grinding or groaning noise when backing up, more often on hills or in the cold.
issues.why: The reverse gear design in the manual gearbox can grind if the clutch is released right away.
issues.next: After selecting reverse, wait about three seconds before letting the clutch out. If it still grinds, have the gearbox checked.

issues.t: Uconnect radio resets, Bluetooth drops or screen glitches
issues.sym: The radio resets or runs slowly, Bluetooth drops calls, navigation acts up, or controls stop responding.
issues.why: Fiat released radio software updates for resets and Bluetooth dropouts, and a weak battery can make these glitches worse.
issues.next: Try a radio reset, then ask a dealer for software updates. Test the battery if glitches come with slow starts.

issues.t: Oil pressure light flashes with oil change message
issues.sym: The oil pressure symbol flashes when the change-oil reminder shows.
issues.why: An instrument cluster software issue, not real low oil pressure.
issues.next: Check the dipstick to be safe. If the oil is fine, ask a dealer for the cluster software update.
